title: Honey never spoils.
explain: Sealed jars found in 3,000-year-old Egyptian tombs were still perfectly edible — its low moisture and acidity keep bacteria from surviving.

title: A shuffled deck is one of a kind.
explain: Fifty-two cards can be arranged in 52 factorial ways — a number vastly larger than the atoms estimated on Earth.

title: Water can be boiling and freezing at once.
explain: At its exact 'triple point' — one specific temperature and pressure — water exists as solid ice, liquid, and vapor all at the same time.

title: A metal exists that melts in your hand.
explain: Gallium has a melting point of about 29.8°C, just above body temperature, so a solid gallium spoon starts turning liquid the moment you hold it.

title: Hot water can freeze faster than cold water.
explain: Known as the Mpemba effect, it's been observed for centuries under the right conditions — and scientists still don't fully agree on why it happens.

title: The human body gives off a faint glow.
explain: Chemical reactions inside your cells produce a small amount of visible light, far too dim to see, but detectable with sensitive enough cameras.

title: Diamonds may rain from the sky — on other planets.
explain: Scientists believe the extreme pressure inside Neptune and Uranus can crush carbon into diamonds, which then sink slowly through the planets' interiors.

title: A neutron star is unimaginably dense.
explain: A sugar-cube-sized piece would weigh about as much as a small mountain — the result of a collapsed star crushed under its own gravity.

title: Sound can't travel through space.
explain: Space is a near-total vacuum, and sound needs molecules to vibrate through — without air, dust, or gas nearby, there's nothing for it to move across.

title: Your stomach relines itself every few days.
explain: Stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve metal over time, so your stomach replaces its protective mucus lining roughly every 3 to 5 days to avoid digesting itself.
